body.statement: Under exactly the model class \(\mathcal M\), can one construct from the sample and fixed class constants a terminating algorithm that returns a finite, finitely checkable witness cover of the exact profile \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\), together with rigorous endpoint enclosures whose deterministic error is \(o(r_n)\), without deciding nonemptiness of an abstract infinite-dimensional decoder?  Such an effective certification result is not established here and remains an open computational question; the statistical band and its rate use the exact profile directly.
body.justification: This records the computational guarantee not supplied by compactness and measurable extrema.
body.gap: A terminating finitely checkable witness cover under the full unchanged model is not proved.
body.consumer: Future work must resolve it before advertising auditable finite endpoint computation.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct a terminating, finitely checkable witness cover of \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\) with endpoint error \(o(r_n)\) under the unchanged infinite-dimensional model.
obligation.obstruction: Topological compactness and measurable extrema do not provide an effective decision procedure for exact model membership or nonemptiness of infinite-dimensional decoded cells under only Sobolev and second-moment restrictions.
obligation.attempted: Taylor--Legendre truncation, positive quadrature, and outward interval subdivision produced outer boxes but did not finitely certify that retained abstract decoders contain model laws while covering every exact-profile law.
obligation.partial_result: The reduced-coordinate image is compact, the exact profile is compact-valued and measurable, and its exact endpoint functions are jointly measurable; these facts suffice for the sharp statistical band.
